input.question: Design a biochemical concentration-response experiment to measure inhibition of Activin receptor type-1 (Q04771) by CHEMBL1078178. Propose an ordered procedure, justify the assay format and parameters, and explicitly identify unsupported conditions; do not supply a remembered potency.

step_cards.action: Prepare a compound dilution series and vehicle/reference controls.

For ADP-Glo: stop the reaction and deplete residual ATP, then perform the ADP detection reaction and measure luminescence.
Prepare the specified cell system, dilution series, vehicle, reference and background controls.
Expose cells to compound under justified culture conditions.
For CellTiter-Glo: apply the ATP-based viability reagent, mix and stabilize according to a supported procedure, then measure luminescence.
Normalize against appropriate controls, fit a concentration-response curve, and report uncertainty and assay limitations.

props.description: Biochemical Binding Assay: Biochemical binding assays (DiscoveRx) and in vitro enzyme inhibition assays (LanthaScreen, Life Technologies) were conducted to determine the binding affinity and inhibition activities of CYT-0387 to Type-I BMPR-kinases (ALK2, ALK3, and ALK6) were conducted. Transforming growth factor beta receptor 1 (TGFBR1, ALK5) was used as a control to determine the selectivity to Type-I BMPR-kinases.
